title: Reject file-directory collisions in research export bundles
body:
## Summary

A real Git package declaring `.research-export.json/input.dat` currently exports and passes `check`, then fails extraction: the input requires `.research-export.json` to be a directory, while the export receipt requires it to be a file. A self-consistent bundle containing `a` and `a/child` likewise passes the checker in either member order despite being impossible to extract as regular files.

Validate the complete regular-file tree, including the generated receipt, before publishing an export and before accepting a checked bundle. Every slash-delimited ancestor is checked against the full file set, so reversed member order, deeper paths and intervening lexical siblings cannot hide a collision. Valid sibling files, distinct prefixes and receipt-first bundles remain supported. The checker still never extracts or executes content.

This is a transport-integrity repair building on Tekalign's exporter in [#3138](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3138), distinct from the Windows drive-path policy in [#3629](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3629). It does not authenticate Git provenance or validate mathematics. No frozen source, source pin, registered manifest or selected result changes. The canonical source/manifest census found no declared exporter dependency requiring historical replay.

The `portable-replay` task is narrowed here to consistency of exported path structure: a successful integrity check must reject contradictory file/directory roles.

Base: canonical main `20ecf2891d80b5acf18d980b2164fb44ea7faa90`, priority revision 6. Complete overlap snapshots checked 347 open PRs, 2,964 closed PRs and 2,454 Discussion records (2026-10-18 12:12–12:14 UTC); no matching collision fix was found. A submission-time refresh found only the unrelated Fourier-tape PR #3640 since that snapshot, and #1166 was unchanged since 12:07 UTC. Canonical main was refetched unchanged. Search coverage is not an exhaustive novelty claim.

## Test plan

- [x] Actual baseline export → check → fresh-directory extraction reproduces the receipt collision: both CLIs print `PASS_RESEARCH_EXPORT`, then extraction raises `IsADirectoryError`.
- [x] The five new regression methods against canonical production produce eight failing collision cases; valid controls pass.
- [x] Existing exporter tests plus five new CLI/Git/extraction regressions: 14 tests pass with warnings treated as errors, both normally and under optimized Python.
- [x] New controls include both file/member orders, deep descendants, intervening lexical siblings, the receipt namespace, no output/temp residue on rejection, valid shared-directory siblings, receipt-like prefix siblings, and shuffled/receipt-first valid bundles.
- [x] The production patch from pending #3629 applies cleanly; all 19 combined exporter regression methods pass.
- [x] Separate same-session reviewer reproduces the baseline and verifies the repair; `git diff --check` passes.
- [ ] Hosted CI and native Windows execution; no full historical mathematical replay is claimed.

Run from the repository root (tested on macOS arm64, CPython 3.12.14, Git 2.54.0):

```sh
python3.12 -W error -B -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_research_export*.py' -v
python3.12 -O -W error -B -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_research_export*.py' -v
git diff --check
```

Prepared for roger-sato with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in diagnosis, implementation, regression tests and writing. Apache-2.0. Same-session agent review is not independent human acceptance.
